Guide

A pocket guide

The decisions that matter, on one page, with a link to the longer explanation.

Findings

Start around six months, with iron and the main allergens. Keep milk feeds. Move texture on. Eat together. Repeat refused foods calmly.
Leave out honey, added salt, added sugar, and whole nuts. Leave out juice, rice drinks, ham, stock cubes, and hard round foods.
Ask a clinician before peanut if eczema is severe or egg allergy is already known. Ask the same day if breathing, colour, or responsiveness change after a food.

Do

Wait until the baby is developing the skills to eat, and start by about six months, not before four. Offer meat, lentils, beans, egg, or fortified cereal early. Offer peanut, egg, milk, wheat, sesame, fish, and soy in safe textures and keep them in the week once tolerated. Sit the baby upright. Add a little oil. Use herbs. Freeze unsalted extras.

Read the pages on timing, allergens, and how meals happen if you want the reasoning rather than the list.

Do not

Do not add salt or sugar. Do not give honey before one year. Do not give whole nuts, whole grapes, popcorn, or thick nut butter. Do not give rice drinks to a child under five. Do not use cow’s milk as the main drink before one. Do not serve liver more than once a week. Do not keep a raw herb paste for a week or store garlic in oil. Do not feed from a screen or bargain with dessert.

Party cakes, chocolate bars, and crisp granola are occasional foods for older toddlers, and several familiar versions are the wrong texture or the wrong sweetener for a baby. The recipe pages say what was changed and why.

Ask someone

Before the first peanut taste if the baby has severe eczema or an egg allergy. If growth is faltering. If you are feeding a vegan diet. If a food caused widespread hives, swelling, breathing difficulty, or floppiness: that last group is an emergency service, not a next-week appointment.

This site is an evidence-checked companion inspired by a Hungarian weaning book. It is not that book, and it is not a personal medical opinion on your child.
